newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW-Gillette looks to Duracell for spark.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Gillette looks to Duracell for spark.

text.p: Each year the world uses 20 billion razor blades and 21 billion batteries and Gillette Chief Executive Officer Alfred Zeien wants them all to be his.

Zeien and Duracell International CEO Charles Perrin, in an interview with Reuters on Monday, spoke of expanding their marketshare, adding products, increasing distribution and consolidating facilities, but declined to comment on a Securities and Exchange Commission lawsuit filed earlier in the day.

A lawsuit filed in U.S. District Court in Manhattan Federal Court alleged that unknown parties bought 1,700 call options on Duracell in the days before the September 12 merger from accounts in Switzerland and the Bahamas designed to conceal their identities. A call option gives an investor the right to buy the stock at a set price.
But Zeien wanted to talk about rechargeables -- the new and growing frontier that will add some spark to Gillette's bottom line.
He noted that the world market for rechargeable batteries, used in laptops, tape players, camcorders and other everyday objects is expected to grow to $5 billion by the year 2000 from $2 billion now.
The first product the new Gillette-owned Duracell group will probably introduce "will be in the rechargeable area," Zeien added.
Discussing the technologies involved, Zeien said: "It's not a sure thing...it's not a shoe-in. But we do that all the time when we introduce a new product."
"I still expect that to happen," he said.
Perrin, who will be an executive vice president at Gillette and in line to succeed Zeien, said he too expected an acquisition within the next two weeks.
"We still are looking at buying. There are two leading manufacturers of batteries in Korea. We're looking at buying one of those, their trademark, not their manufacturing," Perrin said.

Real growth for both companies will come from emerging markets where now only 15 percent of the batteries sold are alkaline. Duracell is now the world leader in alkaline batteries, but carbon batteries are the norm in developing countries. Gillette has distribution and supply systems in Latin America, Asia and Africa that will afford Duracell the opportunity to crack those markets.
